subject: Cognitive Science
title: Hindsight Bias
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Hindsight Bias.

hook.text: After the 2008 crash, everyone said they saw it coming. Before? Almost nobody warned about it.

buildup.text: Hindsight bias: once you know the outcome, you feel you always knew it would happen.

discovery.text: The brain rewrites memory to make the past seem predictable. It can't separate what it knows now from then.

twist.text: This makes us poor learners: if we "always knew," there's nothing to learn from the surprise.

climax.text: Keeping a decision journal—recording predictions before outcomes—is the best vaccine against it.

punchline.text: You didn't know it all along. It just feels that way.

quiz.question: What is hindsight bias?
options: Feeling you predicted an outcome after learning it
